advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure admission spend and _record_spend do not both write to the same ledger for the same attempt (single source of truth for per-attempt cost).
evidence: heal.py `_run_admission` calls `fixture_admission.run_admission(... ledger_path=ledger_path ...)` on the same ledger file the loop resets and reserves against
fixture_admission.py:224 `ledger.finalize('admission-{prompt_id}', ...)` writes an entry on admit
heal.py `_record_spend` writes an entry for EVERY attempt via finalize/charge_estimate on the same ledger_file
The solver comment states the priceable usage row is 'tracked as follow-up work'; when resolved, both writers become non-empty and double-count
advisory.finding: `_run_admission` passes the SAME `ledger_path` used by the outer heal loop and internally calls `ledger.finalize(...)` on each admitted criterion, while `_record_spend` in the heal loop independently records spend for every attempt. Today this is single-charged only because the production solver returns `usage_rows=[]` (admission finalize prices $0 and _record_spend charges the estimate). If the documented follow-up makes the case runner surface priceable usage rows, admission's finalize will record actual cost AND `_record_spend` will also record (its AttemptResult.usage_rows would then be populated), double-counting each admitted criterion against the cap.
scenarios: A future change surfaces priceable per-case usage rows and the same admitted criterion's spend is recorded twice, halving the effective cap

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish an empty gap caused by full coverage from one caused by a routing/registry failure before treating the sweep as a clean success.
evidence: heal.py `_gap_ids` returns `list(_default_criteria(str(repo_root), gate_key))` with no guard on emptiness
An empty `gap_ids` yields empty `attempted`; the loop body never executes and HealReport(ran=True) is returned as success
Litmus: 'the routing/registry produced nothing' and 'every criterion already has a spec' both yield the identical empty-attempt success verdict
advisory.finding: When the gap source returns an empty list (e.g. effective_routing / plan-review registry misconfiguration or all criteria already covered), the sweep computes an empty attempt list, advances the due-stamp, and returns HealReport(ran=True) with no admitted/quarantined entries — a success verdict indistinguishable from 'the routing failed to produce any criteria'. There is no assertion that the gap source actually ran and produced a non-degenerate result.
scenarios: Registry overlay resolution silently returns no routed criteria; heal reports a clean sweep and never mines anything, indefinitely

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a _ProductionAttempter.run test where _emitter_skips_unbalanced returns True and assert the outcome is SKIPPED_UNBALANCED.
evidence: heal.py:380-381: `if _emitter_skips_unbalanced(criterion_id, rows, self._repo_root): return AttemptResult(outcome=AttemptOutcome.SKIPPED_UNBALANCED)`
test_fixture_heal_heldout.py:246: `monkeypatch.setattr(heal_mod, "_emitter_skips_unbalanced", lambda cid, rows, repo: False)` — every _ProductionAttempter test forces the False branch
search for `_emitter_skips_unbalanced` in tests returns only the stub that hardcodes False
advisory.finding: The production attempter's SKIPPED_UNBALANCED classification branch is never exercised: every test that drives `_ProductionAttempter.run` stubs `_emitter_skips_unbalanced` to always return False, so the added `if _emitter_skips_unbalanced(...): return AttemptResult(outcome=SKIPPED_UNBALANCED)` line is untested. The loop-level fold of SKIPPED_UNBALANCED is tested only via FakeAttempter (which returns an author-supplied outcome), not via the real classifier that decides when a criterion is unbalanced.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a _ProductionAttempter.run test with only non-unminable drift entries and assert outcome==FAILED_REPRODUCE with the expected reason.
evidence: heal.py:389-392: `drift_reason = _drift_reason(...)` ... `return AttemptResult(outcome=AttemptOutcome.FAILED_REPRODUCE, reason=drift_reason)`

test_fixture_heal_heldout.py:285: the only drift-driven _ProductionAttempter test uses `drift=[drift("non-reproducing"), drift("not-inline-admissible")]` and asserts outcome=="unminable" — no case where all drift is non-unminable
heal.py:520: `_drift_reason` fallback `return reasons[0] if reasons else ""` has no test exercising the non-unminable-first path via the attempter
advisory.finding: The production attempter's FAILED_REPRODUCE branch (a criterion whose drift entries are all non-unminable, exercising the `_drift_reason` fallback to `reasons[0]`) is never driven through `_ProductionAttempter.run`. The only drift test supplies an unminable reason and asserts UNMINABLE; the plain non-reproducing → FAILED_REPRODUCE classification and its reason passthrough are untested at the production-attempter level.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Report the live heal outcome (ran/not-due, admitted, quarantined, stopped_for_budget) on the non-dry-run CLI path instead of discarding the HealReport.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py:132: `heal_fixtures(repo_root, attempter=attempter, ledger_path=ledger_path)` — return value is not bound or reported
heal_fixtures returns HealReport(ran=False) when not due and HealReport(stopped_for_budget=True) on cap; both surface only through the unused return value
Litmus: the command's success verdict (returncode 0 + no output) is produced identically whether the sweep executed all attempts, was gated off by the due-stamp, or aborted early on the budget cap
blocking.finding: The live (non-dry-run) `_criteria_heal` handler discards the returned HealReport entirely: it prints nothing about whether the sweep ran, was skipped by the due-stamp (ran=False), stopped for budget (stopped_for_budget=True), or which criteria were admitted/quarantined. It returns 0 in all of these cases, so 'skipped as not due' and 'hit the spend cap and stopped early' are indistinguishable from 'ran to completion cleanly'.
scenarios: Operator runs `rebar criteria heal` before the interval elapses and sees nothing, unaware the sweep was a no-op
A sweep trips the $25 cap after 2 criteria and stops; operator has no signal that remaining gap criteria were skipped
blocking.suggested_fix: Bind the returned report and write a short summary to stdout (or stderr) distinguishing ran=False, stopped_for_budget, and the admitted/quarantined counts.
